Explore a plot with orbit controls, tooltips and selection

Source: R/view-3d.R
view_3d.Rd

Draw a plot in a WebGL htmlwidget, using its mapped scenes and initial cameras. Drag to orbit, use the wheel or pinch to zoom, and select Camera code to copy the current angles into a coord_3d() call. Arrow keys orbit;

  • and - zoom. Hovering a primitive shows its tooltip; clicking selects it.

Usage

view_3d(
  plot,
  data = NULL,
  width = 640L,
  height = 640L,
  panel = NULL,
  link = TRUE,
  selection = c("multiple", "single", "none"),
  tooltip = TRUE,
  elementId = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  fps = 30
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot with coord_3d().

data

Optional crosstalk SharedData whose origData() the plot draws, default NULL. Layers that draw these rows take their selection keys from it, share selections with the other crosstalk widgets of its group, and hide rows that a crosstalk filter removes.

width, height

Widget dimensions in pixels, default 640 each.

panel

NULL (default) shows the whole plot: every panel is live, and facet strips, legends, titles and the other parts outside the panels are embedded as SVG around them (requires svglite). A panel index in layout order shows that panel alone.

link

Linked cameras, default TRUE: orbiting or zooming one panel turns every panel by the same amount, keeping their offsets. FALSE moves the panel under the pointer alone. A group name links the panels and also links this viewer with the other viewers on the page that carry the same name: an orbit, zoom or reset in one applies to all, azimuth, elevation and roll changes add and zoom factors multiply, so each viewer keeps its own view. Linking the panels of a facet_views() plot shown in separate viewers turns the front, top and side views as one object.

selection

"multiple" (default) lets shift- or control-click add and remove keys, "single" keeps one key, "none" disables selection. Unselected primitives are dimmed while a selection exists.

tooltip

Default tooltips listing mapped values, default TRUE. A mapped tooltip aesthetic is always shown.

elementId

Optional HTML element identifier, default NULL. In Shiny, camera changes set the input named paste0(elementId, "_camera") and selections set paste0(elementId, "_selected") to the selected keys.

path

A camera path from camera_path_3d(), orbit_3d(), fly_through_3d() or dolly_zoom_3d(), or NULL (default). The viewer gains a Play button that moves every panel's camera along the path with the views animate_3d() renders; dragging or Reset stops it.

fps

Camera views per second of the sampled path, default 30.

Value

An htmlwidget of class ggplot3d_view. Its x contains schema_version (4), frame (the plot size in mm), chrome (the SVG of everything outside the panels, or NULL), panels, link (whether the panels share camera moves), link_group (the group name, or NULL), selection settings and capabilities. Each panel holds its rectangle in the frame, scene and furniture (schema-1 geometry whose table columns are base64 little-endian arrays, with mapped materials and the alpha_mode sheet key of every face), axes, bounds, camera, framing, viewport, light, background, layers (the source rows, keys and tooltips of its primitives) and, with path, the sampled camera views. Geometry is transferred once; camera interaction and playback stay in the browser.

Details

Interaction follows ggiraph for aesthetics, deck.gl for picking and crosstalk for linked selection. Every _3d layer accepts two extra aesthetics: tooltip, the text shown on hover, and data_id, the selection key; rows that share a key are selected together, across layers. Without a tooltip mapping, the tooltip lists the mapped aesthetics of the row under the pointer. Without a data_id, each row of each layer is its own key, written "<layer>:<row>". Map these aesthetics in ggplot2::ggplot() when a layer comes from ggplot2 itself, whose layer constructors do not know them.

The browser holds one interleaved vertex buffer per primitive kind (faces, stroke segments, marker footprints) and identifies the primitive under the pointer from an offscreen id image, by the same primitive_id the raster backend returns in its id buffer.

Requires htmlwidgets and a browser with WebGL 2. Opaque geometry uses a depth buffer. Transparent geometry uses weighted blended order-independent transparency in linear light, an approximation requiring WebGL 2's EXT_color_buffer_float extension. Faces drawn with alpha_mode = "surface" enter it once per sheet: a depth pass per sheet keeps only the nearest fragment of each sheet, so a sheet folding over itself does not darken while other sheets show through it. Sheets whose screen extents do not overlap share a pass; past 32 passes, the remaining sheets blend face by face. Strokes and markers widen to their physical size in the vertex shader, and face lighting uses the same linear-light colour calculation as static output. Text uses plain browser text, with whole-anchor visibility for scene labels. Furniture and its labels rotate with the camera. The widget element receives ggplot3d:camera, ggplot3d:hover and ggplot3d:select events. No external scripts load.

A discrete tooltip or data_id mapping does not split groups, so paths and surfaces keep their shape.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("htmlwidgets", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cars <- data.frame(mtcars, model = rownames(mtcars))
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(cars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg, z = hp,
      colour = factor(cyl), tooltip = model, data_id = model)) +
    geom_point_3d(size = 3) + coord_3d() + ggplot2::facet_wrap(~am)
  view_3d(p, width = 720, height = 400)
}
if (requireNamespace("htmlwidgets", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("crosstalk", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  shared <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(mtcars)
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(shared$origData(), ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg, z = hp)) +
    geom_point_3d() + coord_3d()
  view_3d(p, data = shared)
}
if (requireNamespace("htmlwidgets", quietly = TRUE)) {
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg, z = hp)) +
    geom_point_3d(size = 3) + coord_3d()
  views <- p + facet_views(c("front", "isometric"))
  front <- view_3d(views, panel = 1, width = 320, height = 320, link = "cars")
  iso <- view_3d(views, panel = 2, width = 320, height = 320, link = "cars")
  view_3d(p, panel = 1, path = orbit_3d(degrees = 360, duration = 6))
}
